title: New York as mecca and its limits
summary: Dance and Ramirez debate New York's pace compared with other American cities and why he returned there.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah, but nevertheless, you came back to New York, and

I imagine that... While I've spoken to musicians from Chicago and places like that, and they disliked New York because, you know, they always have said that New York has big-time, braggart sort of attitude... And of course, the pace is a little too fast for them after Chicago. The only thing I feel, having been driven back and forth across the country and lived in different parts, is that New York is a giant metropolis, and you can't judge the whole country by it. You know, it's wrong. It's a unique part of the United States. I mean, San Francisco isn't like New York. Los Angeles is bad, but it's different.
It's a mecca, and it's also a place to avoid if you can.
I mean, it's not the final word in...
No. But what I was getting at is: Now, so, okay, you lived there for three years, slower pace, different attitude. So you come back to New York. You didn't go to Philadelphia or Baltimore. So...
